source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Norwalk campus is a 4 MW facility, small against the utility-scale AI campuses now being deployed.

The published figures are 4 MW of IT capacity and 168,000 square feet of technical space. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, that capacity is roughly 100 racks. The campus holds SSAE 16 Type II certification, which covers audited controls over physical and logical access and qualifies it for regulated workloads.

Norwalk is the larger of Connecticut's two facilities with published capacity, and its 4 MW is half the state's 8 MW of disclosed data center IT load. Connecticut has five mapped facilities in total, so most operators in the state do not publish power specifications. That gap matters for AI because the grid constraint is measured in megawatts, and a state where three of five sites disclose nothing cannot be summed.

What the data does not show is whether this site is a toehold for a larger build-out or a finished regional facility. The suitability score of 49 is a weighted mean of published inputs, and the one named missing input is announced expansion. Proximity to the Northeast corridor and the existing technical footprint are not quantified here, so neither can be weighed.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
